target_name: Committed Hard Spending Under Fragile Conditions
rationale: Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is a mechanical merger of two already-archived signals (Irreversible Capacity Under Demand Uncertainty and Externally Financed Hard Investment Mix) whose gates are averaged rather than reconceived, so it is likely to land between the two parents rather than teach anything new.

This is the archived Irreversible Capacity Under Demand Uncertainty signal re-expressed in raw levels instead of rank space — a pure functional-form variant that mostly trades rank robustness for outlier sensitivity in the sales-volatility tail, not a new economic hypothesis.

Changing the growth window from one to three years on an otherwise identical archived expression is a cosmetic lookback tweak, and the stated diagnosis (measurement noise) is unfalsifiable here since a weaker slope with unchanged alpha would be read either way.

This is a substantive, well-diagnosed repair — converting a level-contaminated volatility leg into a coefficient of variation directly tests whether inconsistency rather than magnitude of R&D is punished — though the ratio will be unstable for firms with near-zero mean R&D intensity and coverage should be watched for that tail.

Coherent and correctly signed, but it is close to the product of two well-established anomalies (low investment / capex intensity and profitability improvement) that FF5's CMA and RMW already span, so the incremental content over the known factor structure is thin.

The re-scaling of the R&D gate by headcount is a defensible mechanism-alignment test, but placing `emp` in the denominator of both legs makes the interaction mechanically loaded on headcount reduction, so a positive result could reflect layoffs rather than accumulating human capital.
